benchmarks.scope_note: International drinking-water guidance; not Georgian law and not an automatic raw-groundwater threshold.
Regulatory text value; Article 1 scope/exclusions, currentness and supply-specific legal interpretation must be checked.
Government-commissioned expert recommendation; not treated here as an enacted Danish legal limit.

FACT: The 2026 WHO consolidated volume retains 50 mg/L as NO3- while the nitrate fact sheet assessment date is 2016.
Georgia Decree №58/2014 lists 50 mg/L as NO3- for nitrate within its drinking-water scope; Article 1 exclusions apply.
The corrected Danish expert report recommends 6 mg/L as NO3- and documents a prior NO3-/NO3-N unit correction.
The 2026 New Zealand cohort reports associations between estimated NO3-N exposure and preterm birth in 735831 singleton births.
INFERENCE: The New Zealand cohort post-dates the corrected Danish expert report and is additional evidence for future assessment, but it does not establish causality or a new threshold.
WHO guidance, Georgian regulatory text and the Danish expert recommendation have different authority and must not share one compliance status.
HYPOTHESIS: A separate legal-control channel and emerging-evidence watch channel can reduce threshold conflation in AquaSignal.
UNTESTED_IDEA: A non-alerting evidence-watch service could notify human reviewers when peer-reviewed nitrate studies or official policy instruments change; its operational value has not been evaluated.

unit_and_matrix_guards: Keep NO3- and NO3-N values in source-native units; never compare them directly.
Do not use rounded conversion factors alone for near-threshold legal decisions.
Apply drinking-water benchmarks only to drinking-water samples with confirmed intended use and legal scope.
Do not use an epidemiological exposure category as a regulatory threshold.
Do not treat an expert recommendation or advocacy statement as enacted law.
Do not infer Georgian prevalence, exposure or compliance from foreign cohorts.
limitations: No Georgian sample-level nitrate data, station/sample dictionary or laboratory QA/QC records were available.
The New Zealand cohort was not independently reproduced by NOEMA.
The Danish expert report's benchmark-dose model was not independently reproduced; it used one study and five exposure categories.
The Danish parliamentary answer dated 2026-11-16 was recorded from official metadata only; its content was not reviewed.
The official NEA 2021-2025 groundwater RAR and acceptance record for contract T-100801 remain unverified.
No independent Georgian legal, toxicological, epidemiological or hydrogeological review was obtained.
